raw_response:
I farm only 2.0 mu, and I am 70 years old, so I will keep things simple, steady, and manageable. I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation because that is what my land, water access, and experience fit best. I have well irrigation, so I will use it to protect yield in the key stages, but I will not push for the highest possible input level because I want stable production and lower risk. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, a couple of irrigations, and basic pest control, because wheat on my land responds well to that and it is work I know how to handle. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, a little more nitrogen than wheat, and simple field management, because maize needs stronger feeding and usually gives me better return after wheat. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me on a small farm and matches the wheat-maize system well. My goal is not to chase maximum yield, but to get a reliable harvest with work and cost I can still manage myself.
